facts.fact: Claude Console is Anthropic's console at platform.claude.com, where Claude Console organizations hold API workloads (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

Anthropic has two separate tenancy models: Claude Console organizations managed at platform.claude.com and Claude Enterprise organizations managed at claude.ai, and a company using both creates admin keys in each (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

A Claude Enterprise tenant has one parent organization that centralizes identity, with linked claude.ai organizations (chat and content) and linked Claude Console organizations (API workloads); a standalone Console organization has no parent (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)

The Claude Console hierarchy is organization > workspaces; workspaces (IDs prefixed wrkspc_) hold members, service accounts, API keys and limits (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
Every Claude Console organization has a Default Workspace that cannot be renamed, archived or deleted (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
The default cap is 100 workspaces per Claude Console organization (archived ones excluded), raisable via the account team (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

Only Claude Console organization admins can create workspaces, and organization users and developers must be added to workspaces by an admin (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

Claude Console workspaces can be created in the Console at platform.claude.com/settings/workspaces or via the Admin API at /v1/organizations/workspaces (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

When a member first signs in to Claude Code with a Console account, Anthropic creates a Claude Code workspace, mints a per-user key there (keys cannot be created manually in it) and rate-limits it separately; it is the only workspace supporting per-user monthly spend limits (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
Archiving the Claude Code workspace disables Claude Code sign-in through Console billing (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

The Claude Admin API is available to Claude Console and Claude Enterprise organizations but not to claude.ai Team plan organizations or individual Console accounts (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
Individual Console accounts must set up an organization at platform.claude.com/settings/organization before using the Admin API (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)

Signing up for Claude Platform on AWS via the AWS Console creates a new Anthropic organization bound to the AWS account, and the AWS Console checks for and prompts acceptance of any private offer (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

Existing first-party Anthropic organizations cannot be converted to Claude Platform on AWS, and their keys and settings do not carry over (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws)
Claude Platform on AWS launched on 2026-05-11 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

facts.fact: Claude Enterprise is obtained via Anthropic sales (https://claude.com/pricing ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)
Claude Team is a self-service plan for 2 to 150 seats (https://claude.com/pricing ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Day-one asks for an engineer joining a client engagement: which surface the client uses (Claude API direct, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Google Cloud Anthropic-managed or Google-managed, Foundry), the organization ID and target wrkspc_ workspace ID, a service account (svac_...) or federation rule (fdrl_...) created by an org admin or a workspace-scoped personal key, workspace rate and spend limits, and whether ZDR, HIPAA readiness or IP allowlisting are enabled (secondary: synthesis of cited docs) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)
The Claude API accepts static API keys (sk-ant-api...) sent as Authorization: Bearer or legacy x-api-key (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
The Claude API accepts Workload Identity Federation, short-lived tokens exchanged from an IdP token (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)

The Claude API accepts App Attest for iOS/macOS apps, issuing 1-hour tokens scoped to a workspace that work with the Messages API only (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
A Claude personal API key acts as the user and stops working when the user leaves (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
A Claude service account key acts as a service account (svac_...) and stops working when the service account is archived (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
A Claude workspace key belongs to no identity and is legacy; Anthropic recommends identity-backed keys or WIF for new integrations (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
Claude personal and service account keys have been available since 2026-08-27 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

Personal and service account keys can be scoped to one workspace or to all workspaces the identity can access; a key not scoped to a workspace must send the anthropic-workspace-id header on every request or the API returns 400 invalid_request_error, and an inaccessible workspace returns 404 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
Claude API keys are created only in the Console, not via the Admin API; the Admin API can only list, rename and change the status of keys (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)

Each key listed by the Admin API reports expires_at, principal (user_actor, service_account_actor or null for workspace keys) and scope (workspace or organization) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)

Claude API key expiration is set at creation and cannot be changed, with presets of 3 hours, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, custom or Never; an organization maximum-expiration policy removes Never; expired keys return 401 authentication_error and cannot be reactivated; available since 2026-07-08 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

With Claude Workload Identity Federation, workloads exchange an IdP-issued JWT at POST /v1/oauth/token (RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant) for a short-lived sk-ant-oat01-... token acting as a service account (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Claude Workload Identity Federation supports IdPs including AWS IAM, Google Cloud, Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, SPIFFE, Okta and any OIDC issuer (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)
Claude Workload Identity Federation launched on 2026-05-04 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
Claude WIF uses federation issuers (fdis_...) to register an OIDC provider (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Claude WIF federation rules (fdrl_...) match JWT claims (subject_prefix, audience, claims map, or CEL condition) to a target service account and an OAuth scope (default workspace:developer) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Setting up Claude WIF requires the admin, owner or primary owner role, via the Console Connect workload wizard at platform.claude.com/settings/workload-identity-federation (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Claude WIF token lifetime is 60 to 86,400 seconds (default 3,600); the minted lifetime is the lesser of the rule's token_lifetime_seconds and twice the IdP JWT's remaining lifetime (minimum 60 s), the Console wizard prefills 600 s, and JWTs with a jti are single-use by default (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Anthropic SDKs use WIF when ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID, ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID, ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID, ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID and ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE are set (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)
A leftover ANTHROPIC_API_KEY outranks federation in SDK credential precedence and silently overrides WIF (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)
ant auth status reports which credential won in Anthropic credential precedence (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

facts.fact: A Claude service account (svac_...) is a non-human identity with no email, password or Console login, implicitly a member of the Default Workspace and added to other workspaces explicitly (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

No separate agent identity type was found in the Anthropic docs; service accounts are the closest thing to an agent identity (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

The Claude Admin API accepts an Admin API key (sk-ant-admin...), created only by organization admins, or a personal/service account key that is not workspace-scoped (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
The Claude Admin API accepts an OAuth bearer token with org:admin scope (admin, owner or primary owner) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
ant auth login --profile admin --scope "org:admin" obtains an org:admin OAuth token for the Claude Admin API (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
The Admin API's service-account, federation-issuer and federation-rule endpoints accept only org:admin OAuth tokens (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
Claude Enterprise Admin API keys are created at claude.ai > Organization settings > API with prefix sk-ant-api01- (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

The primary owner can grant any scope on a Claude Enterprise Admin API key, while organization owners can grant only Compliance API scopes (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

Claude Enterprise Admin API key scopes include read:members, write:members, read:rbac_groups, write:rbac_groups, read:plugins, write:plugins, read:claude_tag, write:claude_tag, read:spend_limits, write:spend_limits, read:analytics, read:compliance_activities, read:compliance_user_data, delete:compliance_user_data, read:compliance_org_data and read:org_audit (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)
Human SSO for Claude Team, Enterprise and Console organizations supports SAML (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)
Human SSO for Claude Team, Enterprise and Console organizations supports OIDC (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)

Claude SSO domains are verified with a DNS TXT record (all from one IdP); setup guides cover Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, OneLogin, JumpCloud, Duo and Ping, and admins can toggle Require SSO for Claude and Require SSO for Console (article updated 2026-10-13) (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)
JIT-provisioned Claude SSO users get the User role by default, and group mappings can assign roles or seat tiers (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)

Groups with source_type: scim are read-only through the Admin API; organizations with JIT or SCIM provisioning cannot create invites via the API, and role updates or removals for IdP-managed users return 400 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management ; https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)
Plan-level SCIM availability (Team vs Enterprise) was not stated in the docs reviewed (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)
Domain capture is a Claude for Enterprise feature, along with role-based permissions, added over Claude for Teams (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)
Claude for Enterprise adds the Compliance API over Claude for Teams (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Claude Code authentication options are a Claude Pro/Max/Ultra subscription, a Claude for Teams or Enterprise account, Claude Console, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS, a self-hosted Claude apps gateway (corporate SSO), Anthropic profiles and WIF credentials (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)
Claude Code can sign in with Claude Console without creating an API key (keyless) since v2.1.242 (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Claude Code credential precedence is: cloud provider (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY), ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, apiKeyHelper output, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, Anthropic profile/federation credentials, then subscription OAuth from /login (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)
claude setup-token mints a one-year CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for Claude Code (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Claude Code stores credentials in the macOS Keychain, in ~/.claude/.credentials.json (mode 0600) on Linux and %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json on Windows; Anthropic profiles live in ~/.config/anthropic or %APPDATA%\Anthropic (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Admins can force the Claude Code login method and organization with managed settings forceLoginMethod (claudeai, console, gateway) and forceLoginOrgUUID, and allowedProviders (v2.1.285+) restricts which providers a machine may use (e.g. anthropic, bedrock, customEndpoint) (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

The recommended Amazon Bedrock authentication path for Claude is a Bedrock service role (iam:PassRole); IAM assumed roles via SAML/OIDC/IAM Identity Center are also supported with a 12-hour max session (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)

Amazon Bedrock accepts bearer tokens/API keys via AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, with short-term keys lasting up to 12 hours (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)

Admins can deny long-term Bedrock API keys with a bedrock:BearerTokenType condition on bedrock:CallWithBearerToken (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)
Claude Platform on AWS authenticates with SigV4 using service name aws-external-anthropic (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws)

Section B of the Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service (version effective 2025-06-17) states "Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services" (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms)

Inputs and outputs from Claude for Work and the API are not used for training by default, but submitted feedback (thumbs up/down) may be used and is kept up to 5 years (article updated 2026-08-18) (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996868-is-my-data-used-for-model-training)
Team/Enterprise Primary Owners and Owners can disable member feedback via the Rate chats setting (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996868-is-my-data-used-for-model-training)

Per the privacy center (updated 2026-07-01), Anthropic automatically deletes API inputs and outputs on its backend within 30 days of receipt or generation, except user-controlled storage (e.g. Files API), ZDR agreements, Usage Policy enforcement and legal requirements; flagged content is kept up to 2 years and classifier scores up to 7 years (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866-how-long-do-you-store-my-organization-s-data)

The API data retention doc says prompts and outputs are not retained by default except for Covered Models (30-day retention) and that retained data is never used for training without express permission, which differs from the privacy center's within-30-days wording; its date is not shown (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
Claude ZDR is a per-organization arrangement obtained through sales, and each new organization must be enabled separately (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Under ZDR Anthropic does not store prompts or responses at rest after the response; it covers the Messages and Token Counting APIs for eligible features and Claude Code with Commercial-organization API keys (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
ZDR organizations cannot call the Claude API from a browser (CORS rejected) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

ZDR does not cover Claude Console/playground, Claude Managed Agents (except self-hosted), consumer plans, Team and Enterprise product interfaces (except Claude Code on Enterprise's separate ZDR offering), Claude for Excel, Covered Models or third-party integrations; stateful features such as Agent Skills and code execution are No for ZDR but are not blocked (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
Claude Managed Agents is not covered by ZDR except self-hosted Managed Agents (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Claude Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2, Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Fable 5 and Mythos 5 require 30-day retention and are not available under ZDR unless Anthropic authorizes it; the Fable 5 rule applies since 2026-06-09 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
The 30-day retention rule has applied to the 5.2 models (Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2) since 2026-11-09 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
ZDR organizations can enable Standard data retention for a non-default workspace to use Covered Models (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Eligible Claude Console org admins enable HIPAA readiness self-serve by accepting Anthropic's standard BAA at platform.claude.com/settings/privacy (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Claude HIPAA readiness is enforced org-wide, cannot be disabled once enabled, and the API returns 400 for non-eligible features (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Claude HIPAA readiness is not available on Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, or for Claude Code via API; Foundry is eligible with a BAA and Azure HIPAA configuration (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
Claude Code ZDR is a separate offering available to qualified Claude for Enterprise accounts via sales and enabled per organization (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention)
Claude Code ZDR disables cloud sessions, Claude Tag, artifacts in Claude Code, Claude Docs, feedback submission and Remote Control (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention)

Compliance API content endpoints (chats, files, projects, session transcripts for Cowork, Claude Code, Claude in Chrome, etc.) and directory endpoints require an Enterprise Compliance Access Key (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
The Claude Compliance API has a shared limit of 600 requests/minute per parent organization (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)

Owners and primary owners can download a CSV of organization events from claude.ai > Organization settings > Data and privacy, with a capped lookback window and no content, narrower than the Compliance API (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)
Inference hooks provide inline prompt governance on Claude Enterprise (details not reviewed) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)
Inference hooks send each governed prompt to the organization's AI security server before inference, which can deny it in real time (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)
Owners/Primary Owners (and Enterprise custom roles with Libraries permission) use Organization settings > Plugins & skills to control plugins and skills (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/admin.md)

Claude Plugins & skills settings set availability (Not available, Available to install, Installed by default, Required), sync marketplaces from GitHub/GitLab, and toggle User-created skills, sharing, publishing review and security scanning; connectors are allowed separately in Organization settings > Connectors, and Enterprise supports per-group availability via SCIM-synced groups (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/admin.md)

Claude Code managed settings sources in priority order are server-managed settings (claude.ai admin console or Claude apps gateway, polled hourly), MDM/OS policy (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode profile or Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode Settings value), managed settings files (C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json, /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, /etc/claude-code/, plus managed-mcp.json), then HKCU; default behavior is first-wins (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings)

Claude Code managed policy keys include disableBypassPermissionsMode, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers, disableClaudeAiConnectors and strictKnownMarketplaces (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings)

Configuring server-managed Claude Code settings requires the Owner or Primary Owner role (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings)

Only sessions authenticating to Anthropic with an eligible credential fetch server-managed settings, so they do not apply to Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry sessions (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings)
